newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar ends firmer vs U.S., eases on TWI.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar ends firmer vs U.S., eases on TWI.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed firmer against the U.S. dollar after a quiet session on Tuesday but was slightly weaker on its Trade-Weighted Index.
The Kiwi finished the session at US$0.7091/98 and 67.82 on the TWI, from 0.7080/87 and 67.89 at the opening.
The TWI had broken through 68 on Monday, a level some dealers said could cause worries for the Reserve Bank if sustained.
It eased back as the U.S. dollar retreated, particularly against the yen, following comments by a Japanese official that Tokyo would not tolerate "excessive" moves in the foreign exchange markets.
Dealers said the dollar had bounced after a brief retreat below 115 yen, and still looked strong on any dips.

The New Zealand dollar remained bid after the overnight announcement of two Eurokiwi issues: a NZ$100 million five-year bond by KFW International Finance Inc and a NZ$100 million two-year issue by General Electric Capital Corp.
Dealers said the expectation was for continued euro interest. "People are expecting more of the same. Interest rates are still reasonably high," one said.
The session was quiet, apart from some Asian buying interest, as the Kiwi traded a 0.7082-99 range.
